thread:
tara: starting a small experiment to reproduce dup side-effects when token rotates mid-retry. building a tiny harness that can flip auth tokens and inject 429 bursts. anyone want to pair on test design? :wave:

ben: count me in. high level: we should capture idempotency-key usage, which SDKs set by default, and also test when keys are missing.

miko: note: Go SDK currently has a 1s resume window by default; Node is 250ms. that mismatch might explain cross-sdk differences.

chris: proposed test matrix:
1) auto-key enabled vs disabled
2) safe_replay_window = 200ms, 1s, 3s
3) token refresh injected at t=100ms vs t=800ms
4) stream vs non-stream endpoints

tara: perfect. I'll script a loop of 1000 calls with controlled inter-arrival and log duplicates detected by server (server will return request_id each time).

infra-bot: test-run: replay-matrix-2064001122 started on staging (run id: rm-2064-01) :gear:

ben: important: for streaming, we need to track partial receipts. add a message_sequence header so server can say "got seq 1..4". then dedupe on (idempotency-key, seq).

miko: also capture timing histogram of when each retry happened and which retry policy tripped (429 vs network error vs 5xx). those correlate with dup rates.

chris: UX question: should SDKs opt into auto-idempotency via simple config like {autoIdempotency: true} or should we only provide helper util to generate keys? I'm leaning to opt-in default false.

tara: agree on opt-in false. but provide a convenience toggle and a safe_replay_window_ms with a conservative default (500ms). document the tradeoffs.

ben: parity request: add the new config to python, node, and go at once so we can compare behavior under identical harness conditions. small PR per repo with matching defaults.

miko: one tricky case: when auto-key is on and user also provides an Idempotency-Key header, SDK should not overwrite it. explicit wins.

chris: reminder: collisions still possible if users inadvertently reuse keys; maybe warn when keys look non-unique per process. but that's optional.

infra-bot: test-run: replay-matrix-2064001122 finished. uploaded results CSV to staging-buckets/jitter-test/rm-2064-01/results.csv :white_check_mark:

tara: I'll parse the CSV and run a quick summary. initial headline: auto-key + 200ms window reduced duplicates by ~40% on non-streamed endpoints, but streaming still shows partial token repeats in ~2% of runs. digging in.

ben: great. for streaming, we might need to change resume semantics: prefer reconnect+restart instead of resume after window expires. or require explicit application-level seqs to avoid ambiguous partial replays.

miko: can we also test full-jitter vs equal-jitter vs decorrelated jitter? those affect burst behavior. add to matrix if not heavy.

tara: adding it. will open a draft PR with harness + proposed SDK flags. tagging @eng-platform for rollout guidance. thanks all :rocket:
thread_summary: design and run of a jitter/replay experiment to measure duplicate requests across SDKs under token rotations and 429 bursts; decisions around auto-idempotency opt-in, safe_replay_window defaults, streaming partial-replay handling, and SDK parity testing
